title: How to use the two-source system
text: Use RPG Site as the chronological completion spine: advance in its order, clear fixed items, Mini Medals, fragments, monsters, and revisit checks before moving on. Use Game8 as the optimization overlay for builds, vocation prerequisites, equipment tiers, farming, hearts, bosses, and achievement cross-checks. When they differ, retain both claims with source provenance and resolve based on the player's exact checkpoint.

title: Alltrades is the first major build inflection
text: Alltrades Abbey is the point where deliberate vocation planning becomes central. Physical routes can start Warrior and Martial Artist toward Gladiator, while Mage plus Priest opens Sage. After the present-day sequence, the Career Sphere lets the party change vocations remotely. Completion routing should also backtrack with the Thief's Key immediately after obtaining it.

title: Advanced vocation dependency graph
text: Champion requires Gladiator and Paladin mastery. Druid requires mastery of any two among Sage, Pirate, and Luminary. Hero requires mastery of any three among Gladiator, Sage, Pirate, Armamentalist, Luminary, Paladin, and Monster Wrangler. This dependency structure should drive early job choices instead of leveling beginner jobs randomly.

title: Moonlighting activation
text: Moonlighting unlocks after Aishe joins and enough story progress causes Jacqui to contact the party via Career Sphere. Return to Alltrades Abbey and speak to her. Because Moonlighting progresses two vocation tracks, it should be activated promptly on a min-max run and incorporated into prerequisite planning.

title: Lucky Panel is both completion and power content
text: Lucky Panel matters twice: it can provide strong equipment earlier than shops, and several items are exclusive to it for a complete item collection. There are three iterations across the game and three games per in-game day. Avoid excessive early grinding solely for rare exclusives if a later iteration offers an easier route, but exploit early prizes when they create meaningful gear spikes.

title: Important Mini Medal power breakpoints
text: Mini Medals are not just a completion counter. Notable reward thresholds include Magic Shield at 20, Seed of Proficiency at 25, Miracle Sword at 55, Metal King Slime Heart at 60, Sage's Stone at 65, Uber Gringham Whip at 90, Metal King Shield at 95, and Metal King Sword at 100. Route planning should treat these thresholds as build milestones.

title: Seed optimization model
text: Reimagined uses fixed stat gains per seed, which makes allocation deterministic. Pre-postgame, Klepto Clobber is a high-value repeatable method for stealable seeds. Postgame, The Almighty plus the four spirits becomes a repeatable source of random Super Seeds. Keep seed spending deliberate so the final build can concentrate permanent stats on characters whose optimized roles benefit most.

title: Metal-family EXP route
text: Confirmed metal-family farming areas progress from Metal Slimes in the Roamer Encampment Region and Highendreigh Tower to Liquid Metal Slimes in Heavy Metal Hole and The Beacon, Metal King Slimes in La Bravoure and Hubble present regions, and Platinum King Jewel in Yet Another World. Ruff's Whistle can speed encounter generation, while Easy Going can raise grinding efficiency.

title: Monster hearts as build multipliers
text: Monster Hearts occupy accessory space and can reshape specialized builds. Cyclops Heart boosts physical critical damage; Clawcerer Heart boosts critical spell damage; farming hearts can increase EXP or gold; defensive hearts can reflect, nullify, or reduce damage; postgame hearts such as Numen can enable immediate burst setups. Evaluate hearts by encounter goal instead of a single universal tier list.

title: Postgame completion checklist philosophy
text: The postgame completion layer includes mastering vocations, reaching level 99, collecting all 100 Mini Medals, filling monster and equipment collections, obtaining Lucky Panel exclusives, and clearing postgame challenges. The knowledge base should distinguish 'required for an achievement' from 'useful for power' because those goals overlap but are not identical.
